h1: Types of Necklace Chains: A Visual Guide to Their Differences

content.text: Learn how cable, curb, box, rope, snake and other necklace chains look and differ. Explore chain styles and lab-grown diamond necklaces from I Want Jewels.

Necklace chains differ in the shape and connection of their links. Cable chains have simple oval links, curb chains have flattened interlocking links, and box chains use square links for a smooth, defined look. Rope chains twist links together to create a textured appearance, while snake chains have closely joined links that form a smooth surface. The right style depends on the look you want and whether the chain will be worn alone or with a pendant.

sections.heading: Necklace chain styles at a glance

rows: Individual round or oval links joined in a simple line

content.text: A cable chain is made from a series of simple round or oval links joined one after another. The links are usually easy to see, giving the chain a familiar, classic appearance.
What to look for: individual links with open space between them.Often chosen for: everyday wear and simple pendants.
A curb chain is formed from interlocking links that are twisted or shaped to lie flatter against the body. The links may be narrow and delicate or wider and more noticeable.
What to look for: linked shapes that sit close together and form a flatter surface.Often chosen for: a chain that has visible texture and can make a stronger statement.
A box chain uses small, square-shaped links connected to create a smooth, structured line. From a distance, it can appear more solid than a cable chain.
What to look for: a neat, squared profile rather than clearly separated oval links.Often chosen for: a clean geometric look.
A rope chain is made by twisting or braiding links together so the chain resembles a small rope. Its textured surface can reflect light from several angles.
What to look for: a spiral or braided pattern running along the chain.Often chosen for: wearing alone when you want the chain itself to be part of the look.
A snake chain has closely connected links that create a smooth, flexible surface. It has little visible space between the links, so it looks more like a continuous line than a row of separate loops.
What to look for: a smooth, rounded or slightly flattened surface with a close-set pattern.Often chosen for: a sleek look, especially without a large pendant.
A Figaro chain has a repeating pattern of smaller links followed by a longer link. The pattern makes it easy to distinguish from chains with identical links throughout.
What to look for: a regular sequence, often two or three short links followed by one longer link.Often chosen for: a patterned chain with a recognisable rhythm.
A paperclip chain uses elongated oval links connected in a repeated open-link pattern. The shape can look modern and graphic, especially when the links are larger.
What to look for: long, narrow links with visible openings.Often chosen for: a contemporary chain that can be worn alone or styled in layers.
A wheat chain uses interwoven links that create a braided or woven appearance. The connected pattern gives it more detail than a simple cable chain.
What to look for: small links woven together in a repeating, textured pattern.Often chosen for: a more decorative chain with a woven finish.
The chain style describes how the links are constructed. It is different from the necklace’s overall design.

For example, a necklace can have a fine chain with a solitaire pendant, a Y-shaped drop, or several diamonds placed along the neckline. Those describe the necklace’s design and diamond placement. They do not, by themselves, identify whether the chain is cable, box, curb or another link style.
How to identify a chain in a product photo

items: Zoom in on a section away from the pendant. The pendant or diamond setting can hide the chain links.
Look for open space between links. Oval openings may indicate a cable chain; longer openings may indicate a paperclip style.
Check the surface. A smooth, nearly continuous line may indicate a snake chain, while a braided texture may indicate a rope or wheat chain.
Use the product specifications as confirmation. A photo can suggest a style, but the product description or maker should confirm the chain construction.

sections.heading: What chain construction is specified on I Want Jewels necklaces?

content.text: I Want Jewels’ current necklace listings show several different necklace designs, including pendants and necklaces with diamonds positioned along the chain. However, the product descriptions reviewed for this guide do not consistently identify the chain-link construction by name. That means it would be inaccurate to label those products as cable, box, curb or another specific chain type without confirmation.

For example, the [Aurora Sette Necklace](/products/iwjnk0003) is described as a seven-diamond necklace, with diamonds placed along the chain. The product page gives its chain size, but does not name the chain-link pattern. The [Serafina Necklace](/products/iwjnk0012) is listed as an 18-inch necklace with a geometric centre design; its listing also does not specify a named chain construction.

To make this guide specific to the collection, photograph the actual chain links in close-up and confirm each chain type with the product or manufacturing team before assigning labels. Until then, describe the visible product design accurately—for example, “fine chain,” “diamonds spaced along the chain,” or “pendant necklace”—and avoid naming an unverified link pattern.
Browse the [necklace collection](/category/necklaces) to see the current designs.

sections.heading: How to choose a chain style

content.text: Think about how the necklace will be worn:

items: For a pendant: choose a chain that complements the pendant’s size and shape. Check that the clasp and chain are suitable for that specific pendant.
For wearing alone: a rope, curb or paperclip chain can make the chain itself more visible.
For a smooth, minimal look: consider a snake-style chain, if that construction is confirmed on the product.
For layering: compare the chain’s thickness, length and overall visual weight with the other necklaces.
For a gift: check the listed necklace length and the recipient’s usual style, as well as the chain’s appearance.

content.text: The product page should provide the actual length and materials. If the link style is not specified, ask the seller rather than relying only on a distant product image.

items.question: What are the most common types of necklace chains?
items.answer: Common necklace chain styles include cable, curb, box, rope, snake, Figaro, paperclip and wheat. They differ in the shape, arrangement and finish of their links.

items.question: Which necklace chain style is strongest?
items.answer: Strength depends on the chain’s material, thickness, link construction, clasp and workmanship. The style name alone does not guarantee how durable a particular chain will be.

items.question: What is the difference between a cable chain and a curb chain?
items.answer: A cable chain has individual round or oval links joined in a simple line. A curb chain uses interlocking links that sit flatter against one another.

items.question: What is a snake chain?
items.answer: A snake chain is made from closely connected links that create a smooth, flexible surface with few visible gaps.

items.question: How can I tell what type of chain a necklace has?
items.answer: Look closely at the links away from the pendant, then check the product specifications. If the listing does not name the construction, ask the seller to confirm it.

items.question: Are chain style and pendant style the same thing?
items.answer: No. Chain style refers to how the links are constructed. Pendant style describes the decorative piece attached to the chain. A necklace may have a named pendant design but an unspecified chain construction.
